title: I Used the Popcorn-Kettle Hours on the Vendor Who Palmed My Numbered Oil

parts.text: I stepped into the kettle cart at 12:08 p.m. and vendor Bud was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE KETTLE. THIRTY MINUTES. OIL STAYS WITH THE SLOT. I was twenty-seven, fair secretary, holding a checkout that listed our numbered oil. Bud shrugged. "Vendors are the kettle." I photographed the board, the booking, and his leftover kernels on my numbered oil. Then I asked for the kettle log. At 12:16 the cart pinged why Bud's name was on my kernels. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The cart can see Bud's leftover kernels on my numbered oil.

social.video_title: He palmed my numbered popcorn oil on my kettle — Part 1/2
social.description: Kettle cart, leftover kernels, a thirty-minute clock he posted. I logged the oil. Would you have asked for the kettle log?

parts.text: Bud called it season until the cart asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the kernel still. The oil went back to my numbered slot. Bud ran a slot of his own and told the next vendor atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: VENDORS ARE NOT THE KETTLE. I keep my oil in a labeled jug. Bud brown-bags his season. The cart finally looks like a slot, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Vendors are not the kettle — Part 2/2
social.description: Kettle log, numbered oil, and a second line on the board. Was season ever my kernels?
